references.text: The prophet Isaiah speaks of the Lord as one who will feed his flock and gather the lambs with his arm, which can be seen as a parallel to Jesus' care and light burden.
The invitation to come to the Lord for those who are thirsty without money reflects an offer of ease and a gift that is not heavy to bear.
Moses speaks of the commandment not being too difficult or far away, which can be seen as a precursor to the concept of a light burden.
The author of Hebrews speaks of laying aside every weight and the sin that so easily entangles, and running with endurance, which can be viewed in light of Jesus' offer of a light burden.
